title: Dependency injection and inversion of control in practice

videos.script: Open the bookshop's book service. It needs a repository to read books from, and nowhere does it create one. {{service}} It asks for one in its constructor. Something else decides which one it gets. {{constructor}} In this lesson you play that something first. You build the bookshop's objects by hand, in the order their constructors demand. {{by-hand}} Then you let Spring do it, and read its log while it works. The container finds your classes, reads their constructors, and builds them in that same order. {{log}} That is dependency injection, and the inversion of control behind it. {{graph}} You inject a clock, so that the current time becomes something a test can fix. {{clock}} You break the wiring three ways on purpose: two candidates, none at all, and a cycle. Each one stops the application with a report worth reading. {{failures}} And you find out what a singleton means in Spring, and when it is the wrong scope. {{scopes}}
